1.title: Level One - What is the error line?
1.placeholder: Enter the line number and press enter...

one: You will learn to use the grep command to find specific lines in files.
two: The grep command filters lines that contain a specific text.
Use the pipe (|) to send a command's output to grep. Example: cat file.txt | grep 'text'
three: Find the line that contains a misspelled word (a variation of 'public').
The file you need to analyze is the website of the company that uses apache as a web server.
Use grep to filter and find that line!

success.message: Congratulations! you completed the first challenge!
success.description:
You completed the challenge and learned the basics of grep!

Useful options:
-i: case-insensitive search (ignores uppercase/lowercase)
-v: invert search (show lines that DON'T contain the pattern)
-r: recursive search in directories

Grep supports regular expressions: use ^ for line start, $ for line end, . for any character.

Fun fact: the name 'grep' comes from 'Global Regular Expression Print'.

Use cases: finding errors in logs, filtering processes, searching source code.
